_comment: Functional Agent Capability Catalogue -- design update Section 2/3. Version-controlled source: promote a capability only by editing this file and getting the change reviewed by a designated functional owner AND technical validator (Section 2, 'the agent cannot certify its own capabilities'). Every entry below defaults to needs_spike; nothing here has been declared Validated by this file's authorship alone -- see each entry's validation.technical_validation for exactly what has, and has not, actually been demonstrated.

identity.description: Update specific, approved processing-option fields on an existing customer-owned version, to a value from an explicit allowed set.
identity.business_domain: Cross-domain (processing options exist on versions across every module)

target.application_form: Any interactive or batch application's Processing Option Revisions form
target.object_or_version_key: application + customer-named version (never XJDE/ZJDE -- scope.py's universal rule)
target.permitted_fields: Exactly the (application, version, option) triples listed in scope.json's functional_agent.approved_versions, nothing else
supported_actions: set a new value from allowed_values

compatibility.application_release: Any (processing options are a stable JDE mechanism since Tools Release 9.1.4.6 per Oracle discovery docs)
compatibility.customisations: None known to affect this capability -- reconfirm per engagement

execution.mechanism: AIS Form Service Request against the Processing Option Revisions form (jderest/formservice)
execution.commit_boundary: Single field write, single commit -- one operation, no multi-field transaction
execution.expected_side_effects: None beyond the processing-option value itself; the option must not itself be documented as triggering other JDE behaviour on save

scope.environment_constraint: DEV only -- enforced universally, not configurable per engagement
scope.company_branch_boundary: Not applicable -- processing options are version-level, not company/branch-scoped
scope.protected_targets: XJDE*/ZJDE* versions (Oracle-owned templates) -- always refused, universal rule

risk.risk_classification: Low, when restricted to non-financial, non-tax fields as scope.json's never_touch_categories requires
risk.restricted_fields: Any option affecting tax calculation, GL posting/AAI behaviour, or security -- excluded regardless of scope.json (see near-term exclusions)
risk.cross_domain_effects: A shared version used by multiple business processes could be affected beyond the requesting domain -- verify no other story depends on the current value before proposing a change
risk.required_approver_authority: Engagement functional lead for scope.json entry; the story's Application Manager for exact-change approval

preconditions.required_records: The target version must already exist and be a customer-named (non-template) version
preconditions.expected_current_value: Read via read_approved_target (the change's own target only) and recorded as the rollback value BEFORE any write, every time
preconditions.locks_and_absence_checks: Not implemented -- see recovery.concurrency_note; this is a known gap, not a claimed control

verification.read_back_method: read_approved_target re-read after the write, independent of the write call's own response
verification.behavioural_tests: The named test Orchestration bound to the approved change (run_orchestration), never a substitute test
verification.negative_tests: Wrong environment, wrong change_id, tampered value, XJDE/ZJDE target, out-of-scope option -- all covered by prove_the_gate.py
verification.evidence_requirements: capture_evidence with prior value, new value, and test result, every time -- verify_evidence_chain before any sign-off

recovery.retry_policy: No automatic retry -- a failed write is reported, not retried silently (functional-agent.md's own boundary)
recovery.ambiguous_result_handling: Any unexpected warning or side effect stops the operation and is reported, never auto-accepted
recovery.compensation_note: A rollback is itself a write, requiring its own propose_change/approval -- never performed automatically
recovery.concurrency_note: No compare-and-write lock exists yet; a fresh read immediately before write reduces but does not eliminate a race -- unresolved concurrency risk is a real gap, not a false one

delivery.classification: Configuration-data change -- not an object/version transfer; CNC's package/promotion process does not apply the same way a development object would
delivery.cnc_handoff: Configuration rows require an explicit, human-controlled migration procedure per environment (Section 1) -- CNC confirms this value is replicated to the next environment as part of promotion sign-off, not assumed included in a package

validation.technical_validation: The GATING logic (story approval, exact-change hash binding, Oracle-owned-version rule, engagement scope, evidence chain) is real, working code, proven end-to-end in prove_the_gate.py -- see evidence_references. The ACTUAL JDE write (the AIS Form Service Request payload) is NOT implemented: ais_client.py's FSR_SET_PROCESSING_OPTION is None, and any live-mode call raises AISClientError until the manual FSR-recording spike (README/GETTING_STARTED Step 4) is completed.
validation.policy_restriction: None beyond the universal exclusions (tax/GL/AAI/security fields, XJDE/ZJDE) -- this capability is not blanket-Restricted, it is Needs spike pending the technical work above
evidence_references: prove_the_gate.py (mock-mode gate proof, all 6 checks passing)
revalidation_triggers: FSR_SET_PROCESSING_OPTION populated from a real spike
a real DEV AIS endpoint configured

enforcement._comment: What the execution gate enforces for this capability (capability_catalog.require_enforcement). Only a capability with a complete enforcement block can execute; the prose elsewhere in this entry is descriptive and is never enforced.
enforcement.target: one processing option on a customer-owned version (never XJDE/ZJDE), listed in the company's approved versions with a declared option category

identity.description: Replace the complete data-selection expression on one approved, non-posting batch/report version.

target.application_form: Batch Versions / Version Design, Data Selection tab
target.permitted_fields: The full selection expression (grouping, operators, types, literals) as one atomic replacement -- no partial-clause edits

compatibility.adapter_revision: Not yet implemented -- no mcp_server tool exists for this capability

execution.mechanism: Not yet determined -- likely an AIS Form Service Request against Version Design's Data Selection grid, requires its own spike (Oracle's data-selection-and-data-sequencing docs distinguish saved specification state from a runtime submission override, which the spike must resolve)
execution.expected_side_effects: None to other versions; must not be confused with a runtime submission override (Section 3's explicit warning)

scope.company_branch_boundary: Not applicable at the capability level -- constrained per engagement in scope.json once authorised
scope.protected_targets: XJDE*/ZJDE* versions; any posting version (batch posting programs) -- excluded from this capability's remit entirely, not just Restricted

risk.risk_classification: Medium -- an incorrect selection silently changes which records a report/batch process acts on
risk.restricted_fields: Not applicable (whole-expression capability) -- but posting-adjacent versions are out of remit
risk.cross_domain_effects: A shared version's selection change affects every future run for every consumer of that version
risk.required_approver_authority: Engagement functional lead + the version's business owner

preconditions.required_records: Target version exists, is non-posting, is customer-named
preconditions.expected_current_value: Full current selection expression, read and recorded before any write

verification.read_back_method: Must read from the SAVED VERSION SPECIFICATION, not a runtime submission response (Section 3's explicit distinction) -- a fresh session's read confirms persistence
verification.behavioural_tests: Run the version and confirm inclusion/exclusion matches the new expression on a known DEV dataset

recovery.compensation_note: Rollback is a separate governed write, same as every other capability

delivery.cnc_handoff: Not yet defined -- depends on the execution mechanism chosen in the spike

validation.technical_validation: No implementation exists. This entry exists to make the capability visible in the prioritised backlog (Section 3), not to claim any working mechanism.

identity.description: Replace the complete data-sequencing (ordered fields, direction, grouping behaviour) on one approved report version.

target.application_form: Batch Versions / Version Design, Data Sequencing tab
target.permitted_fields: Ordered field list, sort direction, grouping behaviour -- atomic replacement

execution.mechanism: Not yet determined -- shares the same saved-specification-vs-runtime-override distinction as data selection above
execution.expected_side_effects: Report/batch output order and grouping change for every future run

scope.protected_targets: XJDE*/ZJDE*; posting versions excluded from remit

risk.risk_classification: Medium -- incorrect grouping can silently change subtotal/break logic on financial or operational reports
risk.cross_domain_effects: Same as data selection -- shared version, shared impact
risk.required_approver_authority: Engagement functional lead + version's business owner

preconditions.expected_current_value: Full current sequencing, read and recorded before write

verification.read_back_method: Saved version specification, fresh session, not a runtime override
verification.behavioural_tests: Run the version and confirm output order/grouping matches the new sequencing

recovery.compensation_note: Rollback is a separate governed write

identity.description: Add or update customer-maintained values/descriptions in an explicitly permitted User Defined Code list.

target.object_or_version_key: System code + UDC type, restricted to an explicit per-engagement allowlist of UDC lists
target.permitted_fields: value, description 1/2 only -- never special-handling code, hard-coded flag, or the UDC's own key structure
supported_actions: update description of an existing value

execution.mechanism: Not yet determined -- likely AIS Form Service Request against P0004A
execution.expected_side_effects: None if special-handling fields are genuinely excluded -- see risk.restricted_fields

scope.protected_targets: Hard-coded codes (per Oracle's extensibility guidance) -- always excluded

risk.risk_classification: Low for description-only edits; Medium+ if special handling is ever in scope (explicitly excluded here)
risk.restricted_fields: Special handling code, hard-coded flag -- 'UDC' does not automatically mean low risk (Section 3's own caveat)
risk.cross_domain_effects: A UDC list can be shared across multiple applications/domains -- verify no other consumer depends on the current values

preconditions.required_records: The UDC list (system code + type) must be on the engagement's explicit permitted list
preconditions.expected_current_value: Current value/description set, read before write
preconditions.locks_and_absence_checks: Absence check for 'add' (value must not already exist); presence check for 'update'

verification.read_back_method: Re-read the UDC list after write, fresh call
verification.behavioural_tests: Confirm the value is selectable where the UDC is consumed in DEV

recovery.compensation_note: Rollback is a separate governed write

validation.policy_restriction: Deletion and special-handling changes are excluded from this capability's remit entirely (see near-term exclusions), not merely Restricted pending review

identity.description: Update one concrete, low-risk constants or setup-master field on an explicit allowlist, chosen from the pilot -- not blanket constants/master-data access.

target.application_form: Not yet chosen -- Section 3 requires selecting one concrete application and field allowlist before this can move past Needs spike

scope.company_branch_boundary: Explicit company/branch scope required where applicable (Section 3)

risk.risk_classification: Not yet assessed -- constants/master data can have wide-reaching effects, so this stays Needs spike until a narrow field is chosen and proven low-risk
risk.restricted_fields: Everything, until a specific allowlist is chosen
risk.required_approver_authority: Engagement functional lead, likely plus a second technical validator given the risk class

recovery.compensation_note: Rollback is a separate governed write

delivery.classification: Configuration-data change (presumed; reconfirm once a target is chosen)

validation.technical_validation: No implementation exists, and no concrete field allowlist has even been chosen yet -- this is the least-defined entry in the catalogue on purpose (Section 3 explicitly defers the choice to the pilot backlog).
validation.policy_restriction: Blanket constants/master-data access is explicitly excluded from any future promotion -- only a narrow, named allowlist can ever be considered
revalidation_triggers: a concrete application + field allowlist is chosen from the pilot backlog

identity.description: Create a customer-defined document type from an approved template.
identity.business_domain: Order-to-cash / procure-to-pay, depending on the document type

target.object_or_version_key: Customer-defined document type code, from an approved template
target.permitted_fields: Not yet defined -- full resulting record needs scrutiny, not just the fields directly set

execution.expected_side_effects: Copying a template is still a change to the COMPLETE resulting configuration (Section 3) -- inherited accounting/inventory/tax behaviour must be enumerated, not assumed inert

scope.protected_targets: Oracle-delivered document types -- never modified, only copied from

risk.risk_classification: Medium-High -- document types can control accounting and inventory behaviour
risk.required_approver_authority: Engagement functional lead + a technical validator given the accounting/inventory exposure

preconditions.required_records: An approved template document type to copy from
preconditions.dependencies: Coupled line-type setup (see line_type_definition) may be required before this is usable end to end
preconditions.locks_and_absence_checks: The target document type code must not already exist

verification.behavioural_tests: Full resulting record inspection, not just the copied fields

recovery.compensation_note: Rollback is a separate governed write

delivery.classification: Configuration-data change (setup record) -- reconfirm once a mechanism is chosen

validation.policy_restriction: None beyond universal exclusions; kept separate from line_type_definition per Section 2's 'each is a separate sub-capability'
revalidation_triggers: inherited accounting/inventory/tax behaviour enumerated and reviewed

identity.description: Create a customer-defined line type from an approved template.
identity.business_domain: Order-to-cash / procure-to-pay, depending on the line type

target.object_or_version_key: Customer-defined line type code, from an approved template
target.permitted_fields: Not yet defined -- ledger and inventory effect flags require explicit scrutiny (Section 3)

execution.expected_side_effects: Line types can control ledger and inventory effects directly -- an unsafe variant (e.g. one that posts to GL or updates inventory unexpectedly) must remain excluded, per Section 3's explicit warning

scope.protected_targets: Oracle-delivered line types -- never modified, only copied from

risk.risk_classification: High -- ledger/inventory effect flags are exactly the fields this capability would touch
risk.restricted_fields: Any flag enabling GL posting, inventory update, or pricing behaviour beyond the approved template's own defaults
risk.required_approver_authority: Engagement functional lead + a technical validator; likely also Finance sign-off depending on the line type

preconditions.required_records: An approved template line type to copy from
preconditions.locks_and_absence_checks: Target line type code must not already exist

verification.behavioural_tests: Full resulting record inspection, explicit check of every ledger/inventory-effect flag against the template

recovery.compensation_note: Rollback is a separate governed write

delivery.classification: Configuration-data change (setup record) -- reconfirm once a mechanism is chosen

validation.policy_restriction: Unsafe variants (GL-posting or inventory-updating line types outside an approved template's own defaults) remain Restricted even after any future spike -- this entry can be promoted only for the safe subset
revalidation_triggers: ledger/inventory effect flags enumerated and reviewed

identity.description: Configure order activity/status rules for one isolated document-type/line-type combination -- explicit transitions, alternatives, and logging settings.
identity.business_domain: Order-to-cash / procure-to-pay, depending on the combination

target.object_or_version_key: One isolated order-type/line-type combination, explicitly not touching flows with existing dependent transactions
target.permitted_fields: Explicit transitions, alternative next-status values, logging settings
supported_actions: add/update transitions on the isolated combination

execution.expected_side_effects: Changes which next-statuses are valid for orders in this combination going forward

scope.protected_targets: Any document-type/line-type combination with existing transactions dependent on the current rules -- excluded from this capability's remit, not merely Restricted (Oracle disallows deleting rules used by existing records; this capability does not even attempt changes where that risk exists)

risk.risk_classification: High -- status-rule changes affect order processing correctness broadly and are multi-step to test properly
risk.restricted_fields: Not applicable at this stage -- whole-combination risk
risk.cross_domain_effects: Order processing across every user of the affected combination
risk.required_approver_authority: Engagement functional lead + technical validator + the business process owner for the affected order flow

preconditions.required_records: The combination must be genuinely isolated -- no existing transactions depend on its current rules (verified, not assumed)
preconditions.expected_current_value: Full current rule set for the combination, read and recorded before write
preconditions.dependencies: Existing dependent transactions -- a hard precondition failure if found, not a warning
preconditions.locks_and_absence_checks: Dependency check for existing transactions on this combination

verification.behavioural_tests: Test both permitted AND prohibited transitions explicitly (Section 3's own instruction), not just the happy path
verification.negative_tests: Attempt a transition the new rules should prohibit and confirm it is rejected

recovery.compensation_note: Rollback is a separate governed write

delivery.classification: Configuration-data change (setup record) -- reconfirm once a mechanism is chosen

validation.technical_validation: No implementation exists. Highest-scrutiny entry in the catalogue by design (Section 3: 'requires multi-step behavioural testing and stronger dependency control').
validation.policy_restriction: Any combination with existing dependent transactions remains permanently out of this capability's remit, independent of any future validation
